q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-23. Q2 FY2027 earnings would typically be released in late August or early September 2026 (NVIDIA's fiscal quarters don't align with calendar quarters). Based on the research stating guidance was issued on May 20, 2026 for Q2 FY2027, the actual Q2 FY2027 results would be released roughly 3 months later, placing us **very close to the resolution date** — likely within days to a few weeks.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA's actual Q2 FY2027 revenue will fall **near the midpoint of their provided guidance range of $89.2B to $92.8B**, centered around **$91.0B**.

**Reasoning:**
- NVIDIA has already issued explicit forward guidance of $91.0B ±2%, giving a specific target range
- Wall Street analyst consensus is $91.9B, slightly above the midpoint but within the guidance range
- NVIDIA historically manages to hit or come very close to their own guidance (companies typically set conservative but achievable targets)
- The guidance explicitly accounts for zero China Data Center revenue, removing a major source of upside uncertainty
- The range given in the question (99.5B to 115.5B) is substantially wider than NVIDIA's own guidance, suggesting the question expects some variance

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Macro deterioration**: Significant slowdown in AI/cloud capex spending
- **Competitive losses**: Unexpected share losses to competitors (AMD, Intel custom solutions)
- **Execution issues**: Manufacturing or supply chain problems
- **China restrictions**: Further geopolitical tightening beyond current assumptions
- **Demand softness**: Customers reducing orders after heavy prior spending
- **Conservative beat interpretation**: If "actual" results come in at the lower end of guidance due to mix or timing shifts

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-expected demand**: AI capex acceleration exceeding expectations
- **Mix benefit**: Higher-margin products selling better than expected
- **China surprise**: Unexpected revenue from China not factored into $0 assumption
- **Market share gains**: Taking share from competitors faster than modeled
- **Pricing power**: Successfully implementing price increases
- **Customer acceleration**: Major cloud providers pulling forward orders

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Q1 FY2027 actual revenue**: $81.6B
- **Q2 FY2026 (year-ago) actual revenue**: $46.7B
- **Current guidance for Q2 FY2027**: $91.0B ±2%
- **Implied growth from Q1 to Q2**: ~11.5% sequential growth (typical for NVIDIA)
- **Implied growth YoY**: ~95% growth from Q2 FY2026 ($46.7B → $91.0B)

The YoY growth, while large, is consistent with NVIDIA's trajectory during the AI boom. Wall Street consensus at $91.9B is only 0.9B above NVIDIA's guidance midpoint, suggesting high confidence in the range.

---

## Probability Distribution

Given that:
1. NVIDIA has issued explicit guidance of $91.0B ±2% (range: $89.2B–$92.8B)
2. Companies typically hit their own guidance with high accuracy
3. The question's range extends far beyond the guidance ($99.5B–$115.5B upper bound), suggesting room for outcomes outside the guidance
4. Wall Street consensus is $91.9B (within guidance, toward upper end)
5. We are extremely close to the actual earnings release date

The distribution should be heavily weighted toward the $89B–$93B range, with limited tail probability above or below.

**Distribution reasoning:**
- **Modal outcome**: $91.0B (center of guidance)
- **10th percentile**: Below guidance range due to execution risk, but NVIDIA's track record is strong: ~$88.5B
- **50th percentile**: Slightly above midpoint, reflecting Wall Street's $91.9B consensus: ~$91.5B
- **90th percentile**: Upper end of guidance plus modest upside: ~$93.5B

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This implies a range with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

This guidance assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate is approximately $91.9 billion, which falls within NVIDIA's projected range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). For comparison, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion in Q1 FY2027 [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), and the year-ago quarter (Q2 FY2026) brought in $46.7 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
